To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
major liver resection is associated with decreased synthesis of hepatische regulatory proteins, resulting in coagulopathic complications.
partial liver resection results in a decreased synthesis of regulating plasma proteins by the liver which results in activation of coagulopathy and fibrinolysissis.

(i) PH induced hepatic insufficiency leads to decreased synthesis of hepatically produced regulating proteins and activation of coagulopathy and fibrinolysys, (ii) treatment with rBPI 21, an endogenous endotoxin-neutralising protein, prevents t-PA release, and (iii) decreased levels of alpha2-macogolubin may be associated with post-operative disseminated intravenous coagulopathy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new method for the treatment of patients with acute liver failure (ALF).
the study of the pathophysiological mechanisms of the postoperative coagulation and the development of new treatment modalities.
the role of the liver in coagulopathies following major liver resections.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

rBPI21 treatment of patients undergoing liver resection may have a beneficial effect in preventing the development of postoperative disseminated intravacular coagulation (IVC) and that the use of rBPI 21 may be a useful adjunct to the management of patients undergoing liver surgery.

rBPI21 is a promising new agent in the prevention of post-operative coagulopathy following PH, and that the development of post-operative DIC may be prevented by adequate replacement of alpha2-M in these patients.
rBPI21 has no effect on coagulation or fibrinolysis in patients after major hepatic resections.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
rBPI21 is a useful tool to prevent post-operative complications in patients undergoing PH.
the use of rBPI-21 in liver surgery may have important clinical applications.
rBPI21 is a potential new treatment option for patients with liver disease and that the use of this compound in patients undergoing liver surgery is a subject for further study.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the liver is a major organ of synthesis and regulation of coagulation.
the liver is the major organ involved in the production of proteins regulating the coagulation and the fibrinolytic system.
we found a novel role for alpha-2-macroglyobulin in post-operative DIC and a novel role for rBPI21 in the treatment of coagulopathy following liver surgery.
